szoveg_eredeti:
The pressure on artificial intelligence (AI) companies to raise funds is becoming a reality. Concerns about "money vein hardening" are growing at a time when huge investment is needed. OpenAI, a representative of AI companies, said its investment contract amount was less than half of its original target. Antropics predicted that its credit rating could remain in the "speculative rating" even after its initial public offering (IPO). Meta's credit rating outlook has been lowered due to the direct hit of worsening cash flows caused by AI investment.

The U.S. midterm elections and earnings announcements of major AI companies are scheduled this week, and domestic and foreign stock markets are in a "overlapping state."

According to the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) on the 1st, OpenAI has secured about $11 billion in investment agreements so far from attracting investments targeting $30 billion.

It is only 36.7% of the original target. The Financial Times (FT) reported that OpenAI has lowered its funding target from $30 billion to $20 billion.

Corporate valuation also fell $150 billion from $1.4 trillion a month ago to $1.25 trillion. As AI-related stocks continued to sell, some investors reportedly reduced the size of their investment agreements.

The investment attraction is an "outpost" nature that reflects the market evaluation of companies ahead of their listing next year. However, the "red light" has been turned on for next year's IPO for the time being as it has been sluggish in attracting investors at this point when it is imminent to be listed.

The situation is also not easy for Antropics, a competitor who formalized the IPO.

As OpenAI's investment attraction and Antropic's IPO period overlap, institutional investor funds are being dispersed. The FT reported that Blackstone, the world's largest private equity firm, recently informed investors that Antropics is likely to remain in the upper speculative grade (BB grade) without receiving an investment qualification grade after the IPO.

Antropic has proposed a plan to invest more than $800 billion in AI computing infrastructure by 2045. However, if you do not receive an investment qualification grade, procurement costs through issuance of corporate bonds will inevitably soar. However, major credit rating agencies have yet to release Antropic's official credit rating.

Meta, which directly makes large-scale AI infrastructure investments, is also under pressure on its credit.

Standard & Poor's (S&P) downgraded Meta's credit rating outlook from "stable" to "negative" on the 30th of last month. Although the credit rating remained at AA-, it cited a surge in AI facility investment and worsening free cash flow (FCF).

Meta plans to invest between $135 billion and $145 billion in AI infrastructure this year. In the third quarter, FCF turned into a deficit of $2.12 billion. S&P predicted that Meta's FCF deficit will rise to $71 billion in 2027 and reach $39 billion in 2028.

S&P evaluated, "Meta's ability to monetize AI investments is more limited than its competitors." Meta immediately protested. "We respectfully disagree with S&P's claims about AI monetization capabilities," Meta spokesperson Kamran Mumtaz said. "We have significant product and business opportunities ahead of us to support very solid creditworthiness."

The New York Stock Exchange plunged last Friday due to widespread skepticism about AI companies. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 2.86 percent and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 7.20 percent.

"Kioxia's forecast of slowing NAND price growth, which has yet to be reflected in the South Korean stock market, and reports on antique credit risks are expected to weigh on investor sentiment Monday," said Seo Sang-young, managing director of Mirae Asset Securities. However, he added, "Considering that some of them were screened last Friday, the fall is not expected to expand significantly."

There will also be a series of large-scale events that will move the domestic and foreign stock markets this week. First of all, the U.S. midterm elections are scheduled for the 3rd (local time). The policy of the existing Donald Trump administration is likely to change depending on the election results. In addition, uncertainties related to the Iranian war are likely to face a new phase.

AI company performance and economic indicators are also scheduled to be announced. Apple and Palantir are scheduled to announce their earnings on the 3rd in Korean time, AMD, Super Microcomputer, and Asta Networks on the 4th, ARM, Qualcomm, Corent on the 5th, and Lumum and Iren on the 6th. The U.S. Treasury bond issuance and buyback plan on the 4th and the U.S. October employment report on the 6th are also major variables.

[Reporter Shin Yoonjae / Silicon Valley = Correspondent Wonho-seop]
